reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only addresses conventional furnace heat treatment of cold-rolled Cantor alloy, showing stress relief and grain coarsening, but provides no data on laser nanostructuring, aligned grain boundaries, thermal boundary resistance, or heat-transfer enhancement. The key premises about the laser intervention and its effects are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Pulsed laser surface nanostructuring can create a hierarchical, aligned grain structure on Cantor HEA.
This aligned grain structure reduces thermal boundary resistance and enhances heat transfer.
Mild post-laser annealing at ~600°C relieves processing-induced stresses without destroying the beneficial structure.
The treatment preserves or improves bulk structural integrity under thermal cycling and mechanical loading.
Cold-rolled Cantor HEA has residual stresses and a refined grain structure that can be modified by heat treatment.
